sections.title: What it lets your code do

claims.text: The library provides decorators for building command-line interfaces: command creates a Command with a callback, group creates a Group with a callback, argument attaches an argument, option attaches an option, confirmation_option adds a --yes prompt, custom_version_option adds a --version with a custom callback, help_option adds a --help that prints help and exits, version_option adds a --version that prints the version and exits, password_option adds a --password prompt with hidden input, pass_context marks a callback to receive the context, pass_obj passes the context object, and make_pass_decorator creates a decorator for a given object type.

Terminal interaction utilities include clear to clear the screen, confirm for yes/no prompts, echo_via_pager to show text via a pager, edit to open text in an editor, get_pager_file as a context manager for pager output, getchar to fetch a single character, launch to open a URL or file in the default viewer, pause to wait for a key press, progressbar to show a progress bar while iterating, prompt for user input, secho to print styled text, style to apply ANSI styles, and unstyle to remove ANSI styling.
Utility functions provide echo to print a message with a newline, format_filename to format a filename for display, and get_app_dir to get the application config directory.
The wrap_text function in formatting intelligently wraps text.
The get_current_context function returns the current click context.
The library defines ten public exceptions: Abort, BadArgumentUsage, BadOptionUsage, BadParameter, ClickException, FileError, MissingParameter, NoSuchCommand, NoSuchOption, and UsageError.
